newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH GOVT SAYS APPROVES SALE OF IPB TO NOMURA-CTK.
newsitem.headline: CZECH GOVT SAYS APPROVES SALE OF IPB TO NOMURA-CTK.

text.p: The Czech government has approved the sale of a 36 percent stake in the third largest Czech bank IPB to Japan's Nomura International, Czech news agency CTK quoted a government spokesman as saying on Thursday.
The spokesman, Ivo Strejcek, later confirmed the deal adding that the sale should be completed by August 1 at the latest. No further details were forthcoming.
"The government has approved the sale...which should be completed by August 1," Strejcek said without elaborating.
Nomura had been widely tipped to win the tender which was fought out between it and Dutch ING Bank NV .
The state holds a 34.48 percent stake in IPB through the privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), and an additional 4.45 percent via the Czech Post Office.
The government is currently preparing the way for the privatisation of most of the Czech banking sector.

On Tuesday, Finance Minister Ivan Pilip said he would submit proposals for further state divestment in Komercni Banka a.s. , Ceska Sporitelna a.s. and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. to the government on August 20.
